brief: A podcast player where episodes are constellations — listened ones glow, series form patterns

dominant_strengths: Constellation metaphor is poetic and well-executed: glowing 'listened' nodes vs dim ones create instant narrative meaning
Cohesive deep-space palette with mint accent reads premium and atmospheric without feeling gimmicky or themed-out
Right rail hierarchy is clean — title, meta, transport, scrubber, series list flow logically with comfortable spacing
dominant_weaknesses: Constellations lack labels for individual episodes, so the spatial map looks beautiful but is functionally undiscoverable on hover/click affordance
Top filter chips (Constellations/Timeline/Categories) float awkwardly in negative space, disconnected from any anchor or container
Series list cards repeat identical structure with no visual echo of each constellation's shape or color, breaking the metaphor's payoff
fix_priorities: Tie series cards to constellation visuals — mini-glyph or matching accent color per series to reinforce the pattern metaphor
Add episode labels or hover tooltips on stars so the map is navigable, not just decorative
Anchor the top filter bar (background panel or align to rail) to stop it floating in the starfield
Differentiate listened-state more clearly with subtle motion or halo gradient to sell the 'glow' promise
rationale.norman_balance: Strong visceral and reflective pull from the metaphor, but behavioral usability lags because interaction affordances on the star map are ambiguous.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes — the constellation-as-series concept is legible and emotionally resonant, though the metaphor stops at visualization and doesn't fully extend into navigation mechanics.
